name: Constrained

arrival.name: Meet the arrival
arrival.text: Most new users come from a Meta ad about stress or anxiety and have never used a meditation app. Orient them before asking anything personal, and speak to the reason they tapped.
arrival.source: HDYHAU Sep 4: Meta is 40% of respondents at 6.6% trial start vs 13.9% overall; round 2 A2 (newcomers reached a paywall not knowing what the app does)

proof-early.name: Proof before the ask
proof-early.text: Trust is built before the commitment moment, not at it. Awards, ratings and member counts go where the user is still deciding whether to invest 3 minutes.
proof-early.source: March A3 (the store listing was the strongest pre-app trust signal); Calmer #1; Insight Timer's 5 proof placements

payoff.name: Every ask has a payoff
payoff.text: A question earns its place by changing something the user can see: a reason line for why we ask, and the answer used within 2 screens.
payoff.source: Growth Gems principle 2; 23-app benchmark rule 2 (reason in the header); rule 3 (result points back to what you said)

echo.name: Say it back
echo.text: Read the user's own words back to them. Personalization the user cannot see is not personalization to them.
echo.source: Synthesis #1 (answer echo, the biggest gap vs the field); round 2 A4 (a named result is where 'it understood me' landed); Alex 5:00 ('a major need')

sourced.name: Sourced, dated evidence
sourced.text: Every number carries a source and a date. Claims are stated plainly with a disclaimer where results vary. No 'clinically proven', no unsourced stats.
sourced.source: March B4/B5 (age-specific stats were the strongest confidence builder; ours were dated and unsourced); Anna's citation set; Balance whitepaper 2025

felt-value.name: Show the product before the paywall
felt-value.text: The paywall arriving before any sense of the product was the abandonment trigger in March. Previews of real sections and a named first session stand in for felt value.
felt-value.source: March D1 (12 of 18) and F1 (5 of 6 newcomers); round 2 A5 (content access resolved the try-first objection); synthesis #10

humans.name: Made by humans, shown not said
humans.text: Faces, voices and the handcrafted mechanism answer the 'is this AI' worry without using the word, which plants the thought.
humans.source: Cindy (Sep 2024); coaches prior art; App Store review 'Love that they use real voices and not AI'; 3 competitors sell teacher credibility

reassure.name: Specific reassurance beside sensitive asks
reassure.text: A concrete, checkable line next to the field it protects ('never shown to anyone') builds more trust than any general promise.
reassure.source: 23-app benchmark rule 4 (Strava, Gentler Streak: highest trust ratings in the set); the deck had zero reassurance copy

no-deficit.name: Compassion, never agitation
no-deficit.text: No scare copy, no presupposed diagnosis, always a 'Not sure'. Validate what the user said, then teach. The structure of Calmer's agitate-then-absolve arc is used; its claims are not.
no-deficit.source: Balance voice (compassionate, grounded); synthesis #9; Calmer's dark patterns documented-not-copied

commit.name: A small commitment before the big one
commit.text: A realistic practice goal and a reminder time right before the paywall turn intent into a plan, and make the trial feel like a decision already half made.
commit.source: Synthesis #4 (Insight Timer's praise ladder, cheapest high-leverage steal); Calmer #41; CYTR +24.7% trial starts

keep-what-works.name: Keep what already tests well
keep-what-works.text: The goal screens, the reminder flow, the trial-reminder chooser and the live paywall stay as they are. The redesign is the connective tissue around them.
keep-what-works.source: Alex 4:35 ('keep our goal screens as they exist'); prior-art census (wins came from reordering and framing, not new content); CYTR and ReciMe are baseline wins

voice.name: Balance voice
voice.text: Accessible, grounded, compassionate, realistic. Digits, full sentences, contractions, no first person except 'Let's', no exclamation points, no 'mindfulness' unless we teach it.

trial-anxiety.name: Name the trial mechanics
trial-anxiety.text: Forgetting to cancel is the objection behind the objection. Say when the reminder comes and what happens on day 7 before asking for the trial.
trial-anxiety.source: Round 2 A3 (the trial-reminder paywall was the only element praised unprompted for the objection it targets); Insight Timer and Calmer timelines

proof-density.name: Proof density
proof-density.text: Insight Timer places proof 5 times before the paywall; Balance places it once. Numbers, faces and what is inside are spread across the flow, each with a source, so trust is built in layers rather than at the commit moment.
proof-density.source: Synthesis #3 (5 placements vs our 1); round 2: 4 of 5 Insight Timer testers named the statistics unprompted; March A3

interests.name: Interests, not diagnoses
interests.text: Ask what the user wants and would use, not what is wrong with them. Insight Timer's flow can be completed without admitting a single problem, and its topic chips read as interests.
interests.source: Synthesis #9 (deficit-free framing); Megan's takeaways (Insight Timer, Happier); Insight Timer #6 and #8

dosage.name: Lower the ask before you make it
dosage.text: Show that a small daily dose is enough immediately before asking how much time the user will give. The chart makes the next question feel small.
dosage.source: Insight Timer #16 to #17 (dosage chart placed right before the daily-minutes question)

plan-artifact.name: A plan, not a spinner
plan-artifact.text: Replace loading theater with the user's own answers assembled into a first week. The plan is the visible payoff for every question asked.
plan-artifact.source: Insight Timer #20 (plan summary: answers animate in as checked chips); Happier's plan summary; synthesis headline finding (a plan artifact is one of the four substitutes for felt value)

description: Today's flow kept intact (goal-1 question blocks, three reminder tracks, Creating Program, account before the paywall) with Insight Timer's screens inserted around it, using only card templates that exist in the app today. Animations, the answer-echo plan and the dated outlook become static cards; what each cut loses is recorded per screen.

cards.body: Built from your answers. Your first session is with Ofosu.

notes.why: Static first-week summary on the list template, one card per goal branch. Insight Timer's chips echo the user's own answers; that needs a template.
notes.loss: The user's own picks read back (content, days, minutes, time of day).

cards.how: A static plan card in place of the answer-echo chips.

title: Your Plan is ready.
cards.body: Your first session is 10 minutes with Ofosu, built around your top goal. You'll find it on your Today screen.

notes.why: Existing program-ready card with plain copy and no 'free'-led framing at the commit moment.

cards.how: Existing program-ready card with plain copy.

title: Create an account to
save your program.
cards.body: Your program follows you across devices.
cards.sub: By creating your account, you agree to Balance's Terms and Privacy Policy.

notes.why: Sign-up stays before the paywall, as today.
notes.evidence: Teardown: 'move sign-up after the paywall decision rather than before it, not removal'; benchmark: the deferred account gate is the archetype's norm
notes.ref: Insight Timer #26 (home reached with no sign-up ever)
notes.loss: Sign-up after the trial starts (wish list).

cards.how: Account creation after the trial in the wish list; before the paywall in the constrained version.

title: Where 6 weeks with
Balance gets you.
cards.body: In a 2025 survey of 3,700+ members, 77% said they respond to stress better and 69% reported better sleep. On your own, most people report little change.
cards.cite: Illustrative curve. Survey figures from the Balance whitepaper, 2025. Results vary from person to person.
cards.learnMore:
Balance whitepaper, 2025. Personalization Pays Off: a survey of more than 3,700 adult Balance members. 85% reported improved mental and emotional well-being, 82% feel more emotionally steady, 78% more present and focused, 77% respond to stress better, 69% better sleep, 86% a stronger sense of progress.

Goyal et al., JAMA Internal Medicine, 2014. Meta-analysis of 47 randomized trials, 3,500+ participants: mindfulness programs produce moderate, measurable improvements in anxiety, depression and pain.

Galante et al., Nature Mental Health, 2023. Mindfulness programs reduce psychological distress in general adult populations, not only clinical ones.

Curves on these screens are illustrative. Results vary from person to person. Balance is not a substitute for professional care.

notes.why: The same graph as a baked image per goal branch on textImage. The prototype draws it live; production ships 4 images.
notes.evidence: Round 2 P5 unaided O4 ('could I see the research for this?'); Alex 8:35 to 9:00 (the graph is 'so important'; 'with Balance', never 'Balance Premium'); legal note in the teardown
fills: Copy pass against the web funnel's Before / Day 2 / Day 30 timeline
notes.loss: The computed date and the goal-specific figure in the body.

cards.how: A dated outlook with the survey figure for the user's top goal, and the research one tap away. No 'scientifically proven'.

title: We'll remind you 2 days
before your trial ends

notes.why: Today's Choose-Your-Trial-Reminder screen, kept. Insight Timer's paywall headline is the same promise ('We'll remind you 2 days before your trial ends'); Balance already owns the mechanic as its own step right before the paywall.
notes.evidence: CYTR +24.7% trial starts (prior art); round 2 A3 (the trial-reminder paywall was praised unprompted)

cards.how: Says when the reminder comes before asking for the trial.

headlines.sleep: Fall asleep faster, wake up rested

notes.why: Terminal screen: today's live paywall, unchanged. Insight Timer's paywall ideas live here as notes for Superwall work, not built: the reminder promise as the headline with a Join / Today / Day 5 / Day 7 timeline, an on-paywall 'How can I cancel?' card with the literal steps, a Free-vs-Plus table, a single SKU with no plan picker, and Skip visible from first paint. The decline off-ramp ('Free / No ads / Forever') is not copied: it only works when the free library is the acquisition engine, and a literal copy would tank Balance trial starts. The transferable part is tone.
notes.evidence: Alex 10:05 (stop at the paywall); teardown 'adapt, don't copy'; round 2: Insight Timer's decline into the free app was the only in-session resolution of the try-first objection (P9, P11), and P10 could not find the dismiss control
fills: Paywall reviews: Tracy's is the live paywall's own; the other 2 are from our verified set
notes.ref: Insight Timer #23 to #25 (soft paywall, App Store sheet, free off-ramp)

cards.how: Today's live paywall, unchanged.

title: Prototype ends here.
cards.body: In the app, a started trial hands off to the first session on the Today screen. A decline shows today's counter-offer, then lands on the Today screen with the program locked.
cards.note: This is the constrained version of Insight Timer's package: today's goal-1 question blocks and reminder tracks kept intact, Insight Timer's screens inserted around them, only card templates that exist in the app today. Every screen here is a session.json content change except the paywall and trial reminder (Superwall), Creating Program, program-ready and sign-up (Swift).

notes.why: End card for reviewers.
